utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Are you hearing me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. General Talic, good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I can hear you in a language I can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, together with Denise Gustin, case manager. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Ms. Korner. Good morning to you, Ms. Gustin. Appearances for Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman with Tania Radosavljevic for Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you both. Appearances for General Talic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DE ROUX
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, I am Xavier de Roux assisted by Natasha Fauveau-Ivanovic and Fabien Masson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So that I'm sorry we started a few minutes late, after 9.00. The reason is I was finalising the arrangements for the ex parte meeting that you have asked for. That will be held in this Trial Chamber, in this courtroom, at 2.15, in other words half an hour after the end of the sitting. I tried to find a smaller place but there are some administrative difficulties and it's easier to have it here for all intents and purposes. So 2.15, we will meet here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour having raised it, I should say that for the record, we've asked for an ex parte hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I mention one other matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That is that in respect of the Rule 70 motion which Mr. Ackerman has refiled today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't seen the new version.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. All I want to say is this, Your Honour. Your Honour, we said we'd be able to respond before the break on Thursday. The situation has slightly altered in that there is a meeting arranged with the provider, at the end of this week, with representatives from the Office of the Prosecutor. We would wish for that meeting to take place before we respond to the motion, and therefore, we'd ask for the normal length of time for a response to a motion. I'm sorry, Your Honour, it may affect our response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is no problem, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We would reply next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Next week, we will not be sitting. I will make arrangements for my secretary to keep me informed because I won't even be here, but if you can hand in also electronic copies of the response, then I can have it e-mailed, even though I can have it faxed as well, but I prefer e-mail rather than fax.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. So we can have -- yes Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I -- I need to inform you of a couple of things. The Rule 70 motion is now in two parts. There's an initial part which is entitled "Confidential amended motion regarding Rule 70, its use and disclosure thereunder." And that is -- it's not a significant amendment of the original. There's an additional prayer there that was simply inadvertently left out of the original. And then there is a confidential annex A to the amended motion which contains material that previously was in the motion itself. Once you have an opportunity to look at these, I think you will agree that the confidentiality with regard to the motion itself could be lifted. And I would ask on the record that you lift that confidentiality as soon as you've satisfied yourselves that there's no reason for it to be confidential at this point. The second thing that I have filed -- and in working on it yesterday, it just became clear that this was probably the only logical way to deal with it. I filed a memorandum in support of my oral request for guidance as to Rule 92 bis. And it's a fairly short memorandum. It's only a couple of pages, two and a half maybe or something like that. I've given it to the Prosecutor this morning. And it raises issues that I think we all have concern about with regard to Rule 92 bis. And I think this might be a way to assist the Trial Chamber in trying to resolve some of the issues. So that's the way I've done it. I expect now that Ms. Korner will with that in hand provide you with the Prosecutor's views, which may not be dramatically different from our own. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is right, that we will -- we can deal with that before the end of this week before we rise on Thursday, and we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. So usher, could you bring the witness in, please. And we'll go into closed session first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm at -- we're there. I'm at page 11 of 30 pages of cross-examination notes. That doesn't necessarily mean I'm a third of the way through. It could mean I'm halfway through. But then the numbers will increase a bit, because I have a whole afternoon to think up other things to ask him. But I think -- I think I won't finish by -- by close tomorrow. I'll probably be with him another hour or so on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, then, Your Honour, the only reason I ask is obviously because we will have time on Thursday, then. There are a number of possibilities. The first is that we could go back to Variant A and B. I take Mr. Ackerman's point that it's being litigated at the moment. In this trial, it seems to be a very long and ongoing process. Whether it's worth re-litigating it here until there's some decision reached there, I know not. The other matter is the question of the documents, Your Honour. I'm still -- I know Your Honours weren't deeply enthusiastic, but I've just been going through the documents that haven't been looked at yet by witnesses, although some will be looked at by witnesses yet to come. We could perhaps use the time by simply taking a short canter through some of those documents. Your Honour, I raise that simply for consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We could do that. So we'll -- Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's my understanding that in another version of this Trial Chamber, the Bosanski Samac case, that starting next week on the 25th that they will be actually calling witnesses regarding the Variant A/B thing. And the word I heard was "witnesses." And so it appears to me that it's being set up to be very comprehensively dealt with in that Chamber, assuming that Chamber is able to start on the 25th. I'm not quite certain of that, but that was the original plan. And that that is the first agenda item on their return to work. So it would seem to me that a comprehensive treatment of that issue is going to be done by that Trial Chamber, and it might behove us to just wait and see what happens there rather than spend time doing a less than comprehensive job with it here. So that's the first thing. And the other thing is I just want to repeat that I really have no enthusiasm for listening to Ms. Korner read documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I was going to read them to Mr. Inayat, but we'll see. Your Honour, I simply -- I do simply make the point, I don't -- it is my firm belief from having done a number of cases that contain large quantities of documents, it tends to get lost unless one has a brief look at them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Anyway, tomorrow morning at 9.00. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of March, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m., to
